Maya Patel: Quick question — for routing & quota attribution when a request uses a service key that can impersonate multiple projects/orgs: do we prefer affinity to follow the impersonated project (owner) or the key's parent project? Example: partner uses delegated SA to hit endpoint, we need billing + quota to map correctly.

Samir Khan: My vote: prefer impersonated project for quota + billing, but keep key parent as fallback. That matches least surprise for customers.

Diego Alvarez: Agree, but security gotcha: we can't trust client-supplied headers for impersonation. Must enforce server-side token exchange or sign the impersonation claim.

Samir Khan: Yeah — propose header semantics:

```http
X-Redwood-Impersonate: projects/456/serviceAccounts/svc-789@proj.gservice
X-Redwood-Parent-Key: projects/123/keys/key-abc
X-Redwood-Routing: affinity=zone-a
```

Server validates impersonation JWT (OIDC) issued by parent project.

Erin Cho: Console UX: when creating a key show two toggles: "Allow impersonation" (opt-in) and "Default billing/project affinity" (Impersonated / Parent / Ask on request). Tooltip: "When allowed, requests that present valid impersonation creds can be billed to the impersonated project." Small copy tweak needed.

Lina Wood: For telemetry & dashboards we need stable labels: billing_project, effective_project, key_parent, impersonation_allowed(boolean). That way cost dashboards and quotas can filter by effective_project.

Diego Alvarez: Also add signature verification: require an Exchange token if impersonation used. Otherwise ignore impersonation header and route to parent. This protects against forged headers.

Maya Patel: Sounds good. For rollout: canary behind flag `impersonation-routing` for 10% of requests, add {metric: "impersonation_enabled", tag: effective_project}. Also add fallback policy: if impersonation validation service unavailable -> fall back to parent and emit alert.

Samir Khan: +1. I'll draft the policy JSON and gateway check logic.
